messages:
liam: quick thought  instead of full cut on bad canaries, what about proportional attenuation? dial canary fraction down in steps proportional to severity instead of binary rollback

priya: I like the idea. reduce cascade risk. can you give an example mapping?

liam: example: if p99 is 20% above baseline, reduce canary fraction by 20% of its current allocation, clamp at 1% min. escalate to full cut only if sustained beyond max_escalation_minutes

elena: how do we prevent the canary lingering in a degraded state forever?

marco: add an accumulated penalty counter with time decay. if penalty exceeds threshold, escalate to full rollback. manual override for oncall too

liam: controller owns decision math, router enforces fractions. contract: controller -> router: candidate_id, desired_fraction, stamp, expires_at, reason_code. router must apply decreases immediately, increases after safety window

priya: telemetry needs: p50/p95/p99, error_rate, queue_depth, kv_miss_rate, and a severity_score scalar. keep formula pluggable in controller config

elena: operational concern: single noisy tenant shouldn't force global attenuation. enforce per-tenant burn budgets in router with counters and caps

marco: solver needed for multi-candidate experiments: naive independent attenuation can hurt overall utility. follow-up RFC for a marginal-impact solver

liam: testing plan: traffic replay + KV/mem thrash chaos. start with simulation mode for 24h before auto-escalation allowed. console needs manual rollback and pause buttons

rollout-bot: Simulation scheduled: proportional-attenuation -> canary-2026-sim. RunID: sim-4422009999

priya: I'll own telemetry schema and sampling rates. liam will draft controller API and router contract. marco will write ops playbook for audit and emergency cut

elena: add 2min cool-down between automatic attenuation steps to reduce oscillation. make decisions auditable in rollout history

liam: good next steps. I'll link this thread in the RFC appendix and open the follow-ups
